papers.title: The cadherin superfamily in pregnancy disorders: from maternal-fetal interface biology to translational opportunities.
papers.authors: Zhao L, Wang F, Xia Y, Zhang L.
papers.abstract: Successful pregnancy depends on coordinated cell adhesion, trophoblast differentiation, vascular remodeling, and immune adaptation at the maternal-fetal interface. Cadherins couple intercellular adhesion to cytoskeletal dynamics and intracellular signaling, linking tissue integrity with placental development and the local immune microenvironment. This review integrates human tissue and circulating biomarker studies with experimental evidence, using selected single-cell and spatial studies to contextualize cadherin expression across cell states and tissue compartments in pregnancy. Spatiotemporal regulation of E-cadherin, N-cadherin, and vascular endothelial cadherin supports trophoblast epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, controlled invasion, and trophoblast-endothelial interactions involved in spiral artery remodeling. Cadherin-catenin complexes connect these processes to Wnt/β-catenin signaling and extracellular matrix remodeling, while altered endothelial junctions may compromise vascular barrier integrity. At the intersection of adhesion and immune regulation, cadherin-dependent tissue organization may influence decidual-trophoblast communication and the cellular context supporting maternal-fetal immune tolerance. Conversely, immune-cell-derived inflammatory signals can disrupt cadherin-mediated adhesion. In fetal membranes, macrophage-derived extracellular vesicles promote E-cadherin loss and epithelial-mesenchymal transition, illustrating how immune-cell-epithelial crosstalk can contribute to membrane weakening. These interconnected processes provide a framework for understanding implantation failure, recurrent pregnancy loss, preeclampsia, fetal growth restriction, preterm birth and membrane rupture, and abnormal placentation. We critically distinguish disease-associated findings from causal mechanisms, with particular attention to the limited direct evidence linking cadherins to immune tolerance. Integrating cadherin-related adhesion, vascular, and immune signatures may inform biomarker development and risk stratification and guide investigation of targeted interventions; however, functional validation and prospective clinical studies remain essential.

papers.title: Partner-specific biological interactions in human reproduction.
papers.authors: Glusciukaite K, Didziokaite G, Vidrinskaite G, Kugaudaite G, Bernotas P, Lebedis I, Vaiciuleviciute R, Pachaleva J, Kuznecovaite A, Bernotiene E, Uzieliene I.
papers.abstract: The World Health Organization estimates that 17.5% of adults' worldwide experience infertility during their lifetime, while approximately 15%-30% of couples undergoing infertility evaluation receive a diagnosis of unexplained infertility. Current diagnostic approaches predominantly assess female and male reproductive factors separately, although successful conception, implantation, and placentation depend on continuous biological interactions between the partners. This review aims to critically evaluate the concept of couple biocompatibility as a pair-dependent component of human reproduction and explore its potential as a framework for future precision reproductive medicine. We distinguish individual reproductive factors and interaction modifiers from genuine partner-specific effects, including differential sperm responses to female reproductive tract secretions, maternal immune adaptation to paternal antigens, and maternal KIR-paternal/fetal HLA-C interactions. We further classify candidate biomarkers as partner-specific, partner-interaction, or downstream reproductive outcome biomarkers and evaluate their current clinical maturity. No core partner-specific or partner-interaction assay currently qualifies as a validated, guideline-supported test of general couple biocompatibility. However, integration of defined-pair functional assays with multi-omics, extracellular-vesicle profiling, advanced reproductive models, and computational approaches may provide a foundation for future couple-specific diagnostic platforms. Rather than replacing established infertility assessment, couple biocompatibility could extend it toward precision reproductive medicine in which reproductive potential is evaluated not only at the level of each individual, but also at the level of the biological pair.

papers.title: Epitope-mapped scFv enables a rapid dual-signal (AuNPs/AIEFMs) lateral flow biosensor for selective and sensitive detection of Cry2Aa toxin in agricultural and food samples.
papers.authors: Shen C, Li Q, Liu Y, Bian M, Liu Y, Li D, Xu C.
papers.abstract: The insecticidal Cry toxin protein derived from Bacillus thuringiensis is widely applied in agricultural pest control, yet its associated risks have attracted considerable public attention. Rapid antibody-based immunoassays for monitoring its residual levels have long been a core priority in agricultural and food safety assessment research. Reliable discrimination of Cry2Aa toxin from the highly homologous Cry2Ab subtype remains a major challenge for immunoassays because of their extensive structural similarity. Here, we elucidated the molecular basis underlying the selective recognition of Cry2Aa by an anti-Cry2Aa monoclonal antibody by integrating AlphaFold-assisted structural modeling, epitope prediction, molecular docking, computational alanine scanning, and experimental validation. An epitope associated with selective Cry2Aa recognition was identified, and Tyr106 within the heavy-chain complementarity-determining region 3 (CDR3) was demonstrated to be indispensable for antigen recognition, providing the structural basis for selective Cry2Aa/Cry2Ab discrimination. Based on this structurally characterized single-chain variable fragment (scFv), dual-mode lateral flow immunoassays (LFIAs) employing gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) and aggregation-induced emission fluorescent microspheres (AIEFMs) were developed for rapid Cry2Aa detection. The AIEFMs-LFIA and AuNPs-LFIA achieved visual limits of detection of 7.80 and 15.62 ng/mL, respectively. Spike-and-recovery testing supported the applicability of both lateral flow biosensors for Cry2Aa detection in agricultural and food samples. This work establishes a mechanistically informed strategy for developing selective and sensitive immunoassays for structurally homologous protein toxins while providing a rapid and reliable platform for on-site Cry2Aa toxin monitoring.

papers.title: Investigating the dynamic interactions between CAR-T cells and the tumor microenvironment: intelligent regulation strategies.
papers.authors: Zhu X, Murshed IAS, Li Y, Yin Y, Han Y, Hu Z, Wu X.
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy has demonstrated significant success in treating hematological malignancies; however, its effectiveness is often constrained by the immunosuppressive network within the tumor microenvironment (TME). The interactions between CAR-T cells and the TME are complex and variable, and the regulatory mechanisms underlying these interactions are reviewed here. This review highlights the effect of TME heterogeneity on therapeutic outcomes and offers a comprehensive framework for understanding the dynamic evolution of the TME at high resolution by integrating insights from single-cell multi-omics and spatial omics technologies. This review also focuses on intervention strategies, including nanotechnology-based delivery systems, metabolic reprogramming, and genetic engineering, that enable active modulation of the TME. A conceptual shift from passive resistance to programmable regulation is proposed, in which CAR-T cells and their carriers are engineered to sense cues from the TME and respond through conditional, intelligent regulatory circuits that remodel the TME. This review combines mechanistic insights with translational strategies, offering a cohesive perspective on overcoming resistance and improving the efficacy, safety, and durability of CAR-T therapies. These advancements are expected to accelerate the development of precision immunotherapy for malignant tumors.

papers.title: Alloreactive T Cell Receptor Repertoires and Their Peptide-MHC Targets.
papers.authors: Sharland AF, Paul-Heng M, Mifsud NA.
papers.abstract: Alloreactive CD8 + T cells play a prominent role in the destruction of allogeneic organ and tissue transplants. Allogeneic Major Histocompatibility Complex (MHC) molecules are recognized through three pathways-direct, indirect and semi-direct. The direct pathway involves recognition of intact donor MHC by recipient T cells, and will be the focus of this review. Most epitopes recognized by directly-alloreactive T cells comprise a donor allomorph in complex with peptides derived from endogenous cellular proteins. Cross-reactivity between viral peptides presented by self-MHC and allogeneic peptide-MHC (pMHC) has been extensively documented, and has provided critical information about the structural basis for alloreactivity. While the viral epitopes are well-characterized, knowledge of the peptide component of allogeneic epitopes is currently very limited. The immunopeptidome of murine and now human donor transplantable organs is being defined and constitutes a vital resource for determining the pMHC specificity of alloreactive T cells. In parallel, T cell receptor (TCR) repertoires from organ transplant recipients are accumulating. Emerging methods for linking TCR sequence and specificity which may bridge this gap are discussed along with future research directions.

papers.title: Integrative Single-Cell and Bulk RNA Sequencing Reveals a Pan-Cancer Treg Cell Signature Associated With Immunotherapy Resistance.
papers.authors: Lin D, Li H, Chen D, Wang Y, Guo W, Li H, Wang K.
papers.abstract: Background Regulatory T (Treg) cells contribute to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICIs) resistance in cancer, yet a systematic approach to capture their pan-cancer impact on treatment outcomes remains limited. Methods We analyzed scRNA-seq data from ICI-treated patients to characterize Treg-related features, including patient-level Treg proportions and exploratory intra-Treg CIBERSORTx scores. Treg.Sig, a pan-cancer Treg-associated immune-microenvironmental signature, was then derived from pre-annotated Treg cells across 32 scRNA-seq datasets and further evaluated by patient-level pseudobulk sensitivity analyses. The signature's association with immunosuppression, intratumor heterogeneity (ITH), and total mutation burden (TMB) was assessed in the TCGA pan-cancer cohort. Building upon this signature, we applied and systematically compared seven machine learning and four deep learning algorithms across 10 ICIs-treated RNA-Seq cohorts to identify the optimal predictive model. Finally, 29 CRISPR datasets were analyzed to prioritize resistance-associated targets, with candidate genes validated by immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, and Western blot. Results Exploratory cell-level analyses showed lower intra-Treg CIBERSORTx scores in responders in both cohorts. In SKCM, patient-level analysis showed a higher Treg/CD4 T-cell proportion in non-responders, whereas broader Treg proportions did not differ by response. Treg.Sig was positively correlated with markers of immunosuppression, ITH, and TMB. The optimal Treg.Sig model achieved area under the receiver operator characteristic (ROC) curves (AUCs) of 0.74 and 0.72 in validation and test sets, respectively, and 0.61-0.87 in independent test sets, outperforming existing transcriptomic models in predicting ICIs response. Among Treg.Sig genes, five immune resistance-related genes were identified through CRISPR data; LYZ and C1QA were significantly downregulated in ICIs responders, as confirmed by multiple experimental approaches. Conclusion We developed a pan-cancer Treg-associated immune-microenvironmental signature and, through systematic application of multiple machine-learning and deep-learning algorithms, established a predictive model for ICI-response stratification. These findings support the potential utility of Treg.Sig for treatment-response stratification and highlight candidate genes for further investigation in Treg-associated immune resistance.

papers.title: Leveraging Contrastive Learning for Conditional and Robust TCR Sequence Generation.
papers.authors: Zhou K, Lin S, Xu K, Zhao W, Liu H, Yao X.
papers.abstract: T cell receptor (TCR) initiates T cell activation programs that are central to antiviral and antitumor immunity, and TCR-engineered T cell is a promising therapeutic approach in treating solid tumors. However, the design of TCR is time-consuming and labor-intensive, and computational TCR sequence generation remains comparatively underdeveloped with fewer dedicated models. We propose an encoder-decoder generation framework (i.e., Pep2Tcr) warm-started with pretrained peptide and TCR language models to conditionally generate TCR CDR3β sequences targeting a specific peptide. It also incorporates contrastive learning over batches to pull each TCR toward the peptide it pairs with. Through a series of progressive evaluations, Pep2Tcr outperforms other state-of-the-art methods under generation distribution, hit (independent testing sets), authenticity (third-party prediction), and generation probability (OLGA). Grafting and docking experiments of some predicted positive TCR sequences to the HLA-A*02:01-AAGIGILTV (melanoma antigen) complex showed plausible scores and potential interaction patterns for downstream experimental validation.
papers.venue: Journal of chemical information and modeling

papers.title: Benchmarking Machine Learning Models for Viral Nanobody Epitope Prediction.
papers.authors: Penhallurick RW, Dean S.
papers.abstract: Rapid development of therapeutics against emerging viral pathogens increasingly depends on machine learning (ML), both to generate candidate binders and for structural validation. Nanobodies (Nbs), or single-domain antibodies, are promising antiviral therapeutics, but accurate in silico prediction of viral epitopes remains challenging. Here we benchmark three ML-based structure prediction models, Boltz-2, Chai-1 and AlphaFold3 (AF3), against a curated data set of viral antigen-nanobody complexes deposited after the AF3 training cutoff. AF3 outperformed the other models: success (interface DockQ > 0.23) rose from 33% with a single seed to 50% and 65% with 10 and 100 seeds-per-target, respectively, compared with 18% for Boltz-2 and 30% for Chai-1. Using an expanded data set, we evaluated confidence metrics and found that a strict ipTM cutoff of 0.8, or a combination of ipTM ≥ 0.6 with a CDR3 loop pLDDT ≥ 60, reliably excluded incorrect predictions while retaining most successful ones. We further establish best practices for two AF3-specific capabilities, the choice of antigen multimeric state and the inclusion of N-glycosylation, both of which can be decisive for epitope success depending on the target. Finally, we apply these guidelines to two design problems: ranking a library of VEEV-neutralizing nanobodies and mapping the epitope of the broadly neutralizing nanobody CC3 across homologous alphavirus antigens. These results provide a practical framework for ML-based viral nanobody epitope prediction and design.

papers.title: Angiogenesis-Centered Risk Stratification Identifies CLU and CP as Candidate Mediators Associated With Vascular-Immune Features in Ovarian Cancer.
papers.authors: Dang M, Cheng S, Wang D, Zhang L, Yao J, Peng Y, Xu W, Huang P.
papers.abstract: Background Ovarian cancer (OC) is a gynecologic malignancy characterized by substantial incidence and mortality. Angiogenesis is a central driver of OC progression and therapeutic resistance; however, clinically relevant angiogenesis-focused biomarkers that incorporate features of the tumor microenvironment (TME) remain inadequately defined. Methods An exploratory 14-gene prognostic signature was developed and evaluated using transcriptomic and survival data from the TCGA-OV cohort with angiogenesis-related genes derived from the GO database. Functional enrichment and immune infiltration analyses were performed to characterize biological differences between risk groups. Single-cell RNA sequencing data were further interrogated to delineate cell type-specific expression patterns. Candidate genes were validated in OC cell lines using RT-qPCR, Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and functional assays. Results Angiogenesis-related features effectively stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with significantly different overall survival (OS) outcomes. High-risk tumors displayed coordinated activation of angiogenesis, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), and inflammatory pathways, accompanied by a distinct immune remodeling profile. Integrative transcriptomic profiling and literature review highlighted clusterin (CLU) and ceruloplasmin (CP) as candidate mediators associated with angiogenesis-driven risk. Both genes were upregulated in OC tissues and cell lines, and their silencing significantly suppressed cell proliferation, migration, and EMT-associated marker expression. Conclusions This study establishes an exploratory angiogenesis-centered prognostic framework for OC and identifies CLU and CP as candidate mediators associated with progression-related cellular phenotypes in vitro. These findings highlight the biological relevance of CLU and CP in angiogenesis-associated phenotypes and provide insights into vascular-immune features of OC.

papers.title: The Predictive and Prognostic Value of ADAM28 Expression in Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma Patients.
papers.authors: Cai H, Lin J, Su R, Weifeng Lv, Guan X, Huang S, Chen J, Zhuo X, Zhang J, Xie X.
papers.abstract: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is an aggressive and common subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma. Although ADAM28 is expressed in various cancers, it is considered a gene with ambivalent prognosis, and its association with clinical outcomes in DLBCL requires further investigation. This study aimed to elucidate the association between ADAM28 expression and survival in DLBCL patients. We collected gene expression and clinical data from 952 DLBCL patients in the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database. Multiple GSE datasets demonstrated that DLBCL patients with high ADAM28 expression had significantly better prognosis than those with low expression (OS and PFS, p < 0.05). Similarly, among patients treated with R-CHOP and those achieving complete remission or partial remission after chemotherapy, high ADAM28 expression was also associated with significantly better prognosis. Furthermore, we constructed a prognostic model for DLBCL patients based on ADAM28 expression and clinical data, which demonstrated good performance. Single-cell transcriptomic profiling revealed cellular heterogeneity within the DLBCL tumor microenvironment; ADAM28 was highly expressed in B cells (including malignant B cells) and was significantly enriched in immune-related pathways such as leukocyte cell-cell adhesion and antigen presentation. Overall, high expression of ADAM28 gene is associated with better prognosis in DLBCL patients and can serve as a biomarker for evaluating the prognosis of DLBCL patients.

papers.title: Immunotherapeutic and Metabolic Approaches to Tumor-Associated Macrophages in Pancreatic Cancer.
papers.authors: Sharafeldin AK, Adhami AMA, Khalifa SKA, Scotton-Peters C, Butler A.
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the deadliest malignancies, with a 5-year survival of approximately 13% and limited benefit from conventional therapy. Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), the most abundant cell type in the PDAC microenvironment, drive immunosuppression, tumor progression, and chemoresistance. Although often described as M2-like, TAMs in PDAC are better understood as a spectrum of states, with single-cell studies resolving functionally distinct tumor-promoting SPP1 + and phagocytic, antigen-presenting C1QC + subsets. This review examines strategies that target TAMs through immunotherapeutic and metabolic approaches. Immunotherapeutic strategies include CSF-1R inhibition, CCR2 blockade, CD40 agonism, CD47-SIRPα blockade, and IL-27-mediated suppression of JAK/STAT3 signaling, which deplete or reprogram TAMs and enhance CD8 + T-cell activity. Clinical evidence is mixed: CCR2 inhibition with FOLFIRINOX and CD40 agonists with chemotherapy have produced encouraging response rates in early-phase trials, whereas CSF-1R blockade with pembrolizumab showed target engagement without clinical benefit, and CD47 antibody development has been limited by hematologic toxicity. Metabolic strategies target nucleotide metabolism (DHODH, glutaminase, glycolysis, and the pentose phosphate pathway), fatty acid oxidation and lipid handling (CPT1a and LXR). These approaches aim to reprogram TAMs, relieve metabolic suppression of T cells, and restore gemcitabine sensitivity, although most remain preclinical. Progress will depend on rational combinations of immune and metabolic modulators, biomarker-guided patient selection that accounts for TAM heterogeneity, and improved drug delivery.

papers.title: Revealing HOXC6 Overexpression and Its Downstream Targets in Small Cell Lung Cancer Through Single-Cell Sequencing-Based Virtual Knockout and CRISPR-Cas9 Analysis.
papers.authors: Wu KJ, Huang WY, Chen YY, Chen XS, Chen GQ, Li Q, Li B, He RQ, Qin DY, Zhan YT, Kong JL, Jiang JS, Chen F, Chen G.
papers.abstract: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterized by frequent recurrence and rapid development of therapeutic resistance, underscoring an urgent need to identify stable and reliable molecular biomarkers and actionable therapeutic targets. Homeobox C6 (HOXC6), an important transcription factor of the Homeobox (HOX) family, has not yet been systematically investigated with respect to its expression pattern and biological functions in SCLC. To systematically evaluate differential HOXC6 expression in SCLC; to delineate its cellular origin and functional characteristics at the single-cell level. RNA-seq and microarray data from multiple platforms were integrated to comprehensively analyze HOXC6 mRNA expression, followed by immunohistochemical validation using SCLC and non-SCLC tissue samples from our institution. Quantitative real-time PCR and Transwell migration assays were performed to validate HOXC6 expression and evaluate its effect on the migratory capacity of NCI-H446 cells. SCLC single-cell RNA-sequencing data were analyzed to identify the cellular source of HOXC6, and functional enrichment analyses were performed on genes positively correlated with HOXC6 expression. In silico knockout of HOXC6 was conducted at the single-cell level using scTenifoldKnk, and the predicted transcriptomic alterations were evaluated through differential expression and gene set enrichment analyses. CellChat and scMetabolism were applied to characterize cell-cell communication networks and metabolic pathway activities, respectively. Immune and stromal infiltration patterns were systematically assessed using CIBERSORT, MCP-counter, xCell, EPIC, quanTIseq, and ESTIMATE, while immune evasion-related phenotypes were evaluated using TIDE. Finally, ChIP-seq data were integrated with CRISPR dependency screening results for multi-omics cross-validation. Protein-protein molecular docking was subsequently performed to explore potential structural associations of HOXC6 with ACP5 and ZEB2, followed by a 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation of the HOXC6-ACP5 complex to evaluate its predicted conformational stability. Bulk transcriptomic analysis showed that HOXC6 expression was higher in 202 SCLC tissues than in 127 non-SCLC tissues. Immunohistochemical staining demonstrated predominantly nuclear localization of HOXC6 in tumor cells and elevated HOXC6 expression in SCLC. Single-cell analysis revealed that HOXC6 was mainly enriched in neuroendocrine-like cell populations, whereas functional enrichment of HOXC6-positively correlated genes highlighted axonogenesis, microtubule and cytoskeletal organization, and establishment of cell polarity. Following the in silico single-cell knockout of HOXC6, specific transcriptional alterations were computationally predicted, accompanied by enrichment of T-cell proliferation-related pathways. Multi-algorithm immune infiltration analysis further showed that elevated HOXC6 expression was associated with reduced overall immune and stromal signals and cell type-specific remodeling of the tumor microenvironment, although no significant association with the overall TIDE score was observed. In cell-cell communication analyses, the HOXC6-high neuroendocrine-like cell population exhibited hub-like interaction patterns, with the macrophage migration inhibitory factor signaling axis identified as a major communication pathway. Metabolic pathway scoring further indicated that HOXC6 expression was associated with differential activation of glycolysis/gluconeogenesis and oxidative phosphorylation. Integration of ChIP-seq profiles, expression correlations, and CRISPR dependency screening revealed that ACP5 and ZEB2 were generally expressed at low levels in SCLC and were both upregulated following HOXC6 knockout. Enriched HOXC6-binding signals were detected at the ACP5 and ZEB2 loci, and HOXC6 expression was generally negatively correlated with both genes across multiple independent datasets. CRISPR dependency screening additionally indicated that higher ACP5 expression was associated with a suppressive phenotype in SCLC-related cells. Molecular docking predicted a potential interaction between HOXC6 and ACP5, while the subsequent 100-ns molecular dynamics simulation indicated that the HOXC6-ACP5 complex maintained a relatively stable binding conformation over the simulation period. HOXC6 is overexpressed in SCLC and may contribute to the migratory phenotype of SCLC cells. It may also participate in neuroendocrine-associated transcriptional programs, immunosuppressive features, intercellular communication, and metabolic reprogramming. The integrated regulatory, dependency, molecular-docking, and molecular-dynamics evidence further prioritizes ACP5 as a candidate HOXC6-associated molecule, although the predicted interaction requires direct experimental validation.

papers.title: AI-Integrated Multi-Omics Profiling Uncovers a Myeloid-Derived Suppressor Cell Signature Linked to Prognosis and Therapeutic Vulnerabilities in Glioblastoma.
papers.authors: Ouyang T, Wang J, Yang J, Li M, Zhang N.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive malignant brain tumour with an extremely poor prognosis and myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) dominate its immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. Multi-omics integration combined with AI-assisted machine learning was applied to establish a stable MDSC-associated prognostic signature. We systematically analysed its biological functions, immune landscapes, single-cell localisation and therapeutic value and further validated the core genes via clinical tissue, in vitro and in vivo assays. We obtained 28 overlapping MDSC-related genes and adopted Elastic Net Cox regression out of four machine-learning Cox algorithms to construct a six-gene signature (TIMP1, FOXM1, ALDH1A1, MMP9, NRG1, MIR7-3HG) in the TCGA cohort, with the CGGA325 dataset for external validation. This signature distinctly stratified patients into high-risk and low-risk subgroups with disparate survival. The high-risk group displayed strengthened proliferation and invasion, disordered apoptosis, activated oncogenic and inflammatory pathways, as well as an immunosuppressive microenvironment marked by M2 macrophage accumulation and elevated expression of multiple immune checkpoints. Single-cell data indicated that signature genes were enriched in high-stemness, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and hypoxia, with TIMP1 acting as a critical regulator. Drug screening on CTRP and GDSC2 databases yielded candidate compounds for high-risk populations. Clinical samples verified higher TIMP1 expression in GBM tissues than in adjacent normal tissues; in vitro and in vivo assays confirmed that TIMP1 knockdown restrained GBM malignant behaviours, while its overexpression produced opposite effects. Taken together, this novel six-gene MDSC-related signature tightly correlates with GBM malignant progression and an immunosuppressive phenotype, supports robust prognostic stratification and provides a basis for exploring candidate therapeutic targets that warrant further validation.
